name: Question 15
problem: Find the signed curvature of the curve $y={2}^{x}$ at $x=-1.$
worked_solution:
The signed curvature $k(x)$ of a plane curve $y=y(x)$ is given by

$$
k(x)=\frac{{y}^{″}(x)}{(1+[{y}^{′}(x)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${y}^{′}(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,{y}^{″}(x)={2}^{x}{ln}^{2}⁡2
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the signed curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}k(x) & =\frac{{2}^{x}{ln}^{2}⁡2}{{[1+{({2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}^{2}]}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{x}{ln}^{2}⁡2}{{(1+{2}^{2x}{ln}^{2}⁡2)}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}k(-1) & =\frac{{2}^{-1}{ln}^{2}⁡2}{{(1+{2}^{2(-1)}{ln}^{2}⁡2)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡2}{2})}{{(\frac{4+{ln}^{2}⁡2}{4})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{4{ln}^{2}⁡2}{(4+{ln}^{2}⁡2)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Find the signed curvature of the curve y=2x at x=−1.

a
2ln2⁡2(2+ln2⁡2)3/2
b
−8ln2⁡2(4+ln2⁡2)3/2
c
4ln2⁡2(4+ln2⁡2)3/2
d
−2ln2⁡2(1+ln2⁡2)3/2
e
4ln2⁡2(1+ln2⁡2)3/2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The signed curvature k(x) of a plane curve y=y(x) is given by

k(x)=y″(x)(1+[y′(x)]2)3/2.

First, we calculate y′(x) and y″(x):

y′(x)=2xln⁡2,y″(x)=2xln2⁡2

Substituting these into the formula for the signed curvature, we get the following:

k(x)=2xln2⁡2[1+(2xln⁡2)2]3/2=2xln2⁡2(1+22xln2⁡2)3/2

Therefore, the curvature at x=−1 is

k(−1)=2−1ln2⁡2(1+22(−1)ln2⁡2)3/2=(ln2⁡22)(4+ln2⁡24)3/2=4ln2⁡2(4+ln2⁡2)3/2.
